To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the media-to-lumen (M/L) ratio of small resistance arteries is a prognostically significant parameter, which is increased in patients with hypertension, obesity, and diabetes mellitus.

structural alterations of small resistance arteries are a prognostically-relevant factor in hypertension, and they may be used for cardiovascular risk stratification, as well as an intermediate endpoint to evaluate the effects of antitensive treatment.

the evaluation of microvessel morphology in hypertensive patients, by non-invasive methods, is progressively moving from the bench to the bedside, and that this may represent a promising future perspective in the evaluation of cardiovascular risk in hypertension, and, possibly also as an intermediate endpoint of the effects of treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the prognostic significance of structural alterations of the microcirculation in hypertension.
a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the structural alterations of small resistance arteries in hypertension and in other conditions of cardiovascular risk.
the study of microvascular structure and the relationship of microvascular structure with the development of target organ complications and cardiovascular events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microvascular structure is an important prognostic endpoint in hypertension.

the evaluation of microvessel morphology is progressively moving from the bench to the bedside, and it will be an important tool in the near future for a better stratification and risk prediction of hypertensive patients.
the microvascular structure is a prognostically important parameter, which may be evaluated non-invasively and, therefore, may be used as an intermediate endpoint of antihypetensive treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the evaluation of microvasculature, in particular small arteries, may represent a promising new approach in the cardiovascular risk stratifications, and, in the future, it could be considered as an additional endpoint in the evaluation and comparison of different antihypertensives.

the evaluation of the remodelling of sub-cutaneous small arteries is a useful and promising tool in the evaluation of target organ damage and cardiovascular risk in hypertensive patients, although further investigations are needed to make this technique a useful tool in the clinical practice.
the microvasculature is a key player in the cardiovascular disease, but its role is not yet fully understood and needs further investigation.

microvascular structure is a prognostically important endpoint.
the evaluation of microcirculation is progressively moving from the bench to the bedside, and it may become a new and interesting prognostic marker in hypertension.
